response.rationale: The clinical presentation of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and dermal neutrophilia with eosinophils is most consistent with vegetative pyoderma gangrenosum. Sweet syndrome lacks the epidermal pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and typically shows diffuse dermal neutrophilia without eosinophil-rich microabscesses. Eczema herpeticum is contradicted by negative PAS and absence of viral cytopathic changes.

rejected.why: Negative PAS and no herpetic cytopathic features; HIV negative reduces likelihood; clinical pattern is not vesicular.
Lacks pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and eosinophil-rich microabscesses; clinical vegetating plaques are more typical of pyoderma gangrenosum.
